purpose: Recommended first-game Decks rebuilt from each Leader's full legal v0.6.2 Neutral-plus-faction pool.

decks.name: Forward Doctrine
decks.summary: Create repeated attack opportunities, spend Command to extend victories, and turn tempo into Front Line gains.
decks.openingPlan: Use Forced March, Advance Guard, or Invasion during Opening to choose the first battle. Preserve Command until Rally, Onward, or Rout changes the position that matters.
decks.firstGameTip: Invasion ends as soon as it creates a pending battle, so move one Position at a time. Assimilation is strongest when the contested Territory is the next Territory beyond your Front Line.
decks.opponentWatch: The General can create several attack opportunities in one turn. Track Command and expect larger attacker Reserves when Invasion appears.

decks.name: Holdfast
decks.summary: Prepare controlled ground, absorb the attack, and turn defensive wins into retreat pressure and delayed capture.
decks.openingPlan: Bank or place a defensive card early. Entrenchment, Palisade Wall, Encampment, and Protracted Siege make the opponent fight through prepared positions.
decks.firstGameTip: Do not advance merely because you can. A controlled Territory with Defensive Edge, a prepared Asset, and Command available for Entrench or Repel is often your strongest position.
decks.opponentWatch: The Commandant rewards attacking into prepared ground. Check banked Assets, Command, Landslide, and Protracted Siege before committing.

decks.name: Open Channels
decks.summary: Make attractive Terms, gain cards and Influence from acceptance, and turn ratified Proposals into a repeatable diplomatic engine.
decks.openingPlan: Offer low-Stake Proposals first. Trade Concessions, Good Faith, Nonbinding Resolution, and Détente make accepted Terms productive without abandoning ordinary territorial play.
decks.firstGameTip: Détente rewards a Proposal only when it was already ratified before you offered it. Use early acceptance to create Treaty Articles, then profit when the opponent accepts them again.
decks.opponentWatch: The Ambassador benefits when Terms are accepted and can eventually win through five different ratified Proposals. Read the Proposal before choosing.

decks.name: Procedure Endures
decks.summary: Stake Influence aggressively, preserve political capital after setbacks, and constrain the opponent through repeated Terms and Sanctions.
decks.openingPlan: Keep cards in Hand to support Political Capital. Safe Conduct and Neutral Observers reduce the risk of refused Terms while Censure and Embargo punish repeated refusal.
decks.firstGameTip: The Senator can recover staked Influence by sacrificing cards after a lost battle following refused Terms. Do not empty your Hand before making a high-Stake offer.
decks.opponentWatch: The Senator can risk larger Stakes and recover them through Political Capital. Repeated refusal may establish Sanctions that remain until Terms are accepted.

decks.name: Sound Investment
decks.summary: Build Treasury value, convert cards into flexible financing, and acquire Deeds through a stable two-Action economy.
decks.openingPlan: Use Speculation, Liquidation, Capital Gains, or Compound Interest to establish Treasury and Capital. Financial Capacity then supports setup in Opening and a Faction Action in Denouement.
decks.firstGameTip: Line of Credit is strongest when a card pays part of a Deed cost without exhausting Capital. Compound Interest can grow Treasury after the normal Draw, but only after Treasury already contains a card.
decks.opponentWatch: The Banker turns cards into purchase power and may gain two Action phases through Financial Capacity. Track Treasury value, Capital, and owned Deeds.

decks.name: Hostile Expansion
decks.summary: Create offensive movement, win on the next Territory beyond the Front Line, and convert the victory into Deed ownership and control.
decks.openingPlan: Use Forced March, Advance Guard, and Speculation to prepare the attack. Save Capital or collateral so Hostile Takeover or Leveraged Buyout can follow the win.
decks.firstGameTip: Hostile Takeover is a Denouement Faction Action. Financial Capacity can let you prepare during Opening and still buy the contested Deed after a successful attack.
decks.opponentWatch: The Executive can combine movement, battle, and acquisition in one turn. A Deed owned before the battle can also enable Foreclosure.

decks.name: Field Operations
decks.summary: Use terrain, reconnaissance, and adaptable Missions to operate safely while preserving Intel for decisive interference.
decks.openingPlan: Choose a Mission that matches the current board. Pathfinders, Fog of War, Reconnaissance, and Operational Reassessment keep the route and Mission plan flexible.
decks.firstGameTip: Spend Intel on Fieldcraft when a Territory effect would stop the turn, not for a minor convenience. Extraordinary Rendition removes one important card but must be discarded before other Assets when Asset loss occurs.
decks.opponentWatch: The Ranger can ignore a Territory effect once per turn by spending Intel and can inspect or interfere with hidden battle commitments.

decks.name: Mission Network
decks.summary: Complete Missions in sequence, use Mission Control to avoid setup gaps, and build toward a concealed Special Operation.
decks.openingPlan: Keep a second eligible Mission available before completing the first. Fog of War, Disinformation, and Operational Reassessment create repeatable Mission evidence.
decks.firstGameTip: Mission Control starts a new normal Mission immediately after completion without taking an Action. Sleeper Network rewards planning several future Action effects rather than spending every card at once.
decks.opponentWatch: The Spymaster can chain Missions and accelerate Operation Progress. Watch public Progress and Intel even though the active Mission remains hidden.

decks.name: First Principles
decks.summary: Sacrifice cards deliberately, replace the first qualifying loss through Materia Prima, and convert the Graveyard into a working resource.
decks.openingPlan: Use Dark Omens, Fate's Toll, or Rite costs to place a card in the Graveyard while Materia Prima replaces it. Grave Ward, Soul for Soul, and Rend the Veil turn that setup into value.
decks.firstGameTip: Plan the first qualifying Hand-to-Graveyard move on your turn before spending cards elsewhere. Nature's Altar can begin a Rite during Opening when its Territory and Rite requirements are satisfied.
decks.opponentWatch: The Alchemist gains card flow from deliberate sacrifice and can reuse Graveyard effects. Track completed Rites and cards available for Transmutation.

decks.name: Unbroken Circle
decks.summary: Begin a Rite from a defensible position, preserve progress through loss, and recover the Arcane cards needed for the Ritual.
decks.openingPlan: Establish Grave Ward, Spirit Hollow, Entrenchment, or Nature's Altar before committing to a Rite. Keep an Arcane card whose value meets the current Guardians threshold.
decks.firstGameTip: Guardians of the Circle requires value 1, 2, 3, or 4 as progress advances. Nature's Altar permits same-turn Rite completion only when you control its Territory at completion timing.
decks.opponentWatch: The Spirit Walker can preserve Rite or Ritual progress after a loss by sacrificing an eligible Arcane card. Pressure Hand size and control of Nature's Altar.

decks.name: Final Judgment
decks.summary: Win battles, convert the cleared Aftermath into a discounted Purge, and permanently reduce the opponent's recyclable options.
decks.openingPlan: Use Accusation, Divine Mercy, and Act of Faith to shape the opponent's Discard Pile and build Conviction. Preserve enough Conviction for Final Judgment after a win.
decks.firstGameTip: Final Judgment occurs after battle cards are cleared and does not consume the Purge Faction Action. Martyrdom is a comeback card after a loss, not a way to prevent the loss.
decks.opponentWatch: The Grand Inquisitor gains Conviction from opposing Graveyard entries and can Purge again after winning. The Discard Pile is not safe storage.

decks.name: Relentless Pursuit
decks.summary: Defend prepared Territories, punish attacking losses, and spend Conviction to end the opponent's turn and pursue immediately.
decks.openingPlan: Build Conviction while establishing Entrenchment, Palisade Wall, No Martyrs, or Scorched Earth. A defensive win can convert directly into Relentless Pursuit.
decks.firstGameTip: Keep 2 Conviction available when the opponent attacks. Relentless Pursuit creates no Opening or Denouement before its pending battle, but Terms still occur before Onset.
decks.opponentWatch: A failed attack can end your turn and launch an immediate counterattack. No Martyrs also suppresses beneficial effects triggered by your loss or retreat.
